title: Company information API: automating business data to cut onboarding friction and manual research
summary: Yahia Bakour (Context.dev) explains how a company information API turns a domain into verified brand and business data (logos, colors, addresses, NAICS codes). It covers use cases like frictionless onboarding and enrichment, a quick integration walkthrough, and criteria for choosing a provider. Much of it is product-oriented, but it shows the logic of API-first data over manual research.

principles.text: Auto-populate signup data from a work email's domain to remove form friction and lift trial conversion.
principles.quote: As soon as a user enters their work email, the API fills in company name, address, and industry, creating a frictionless first impression that boosts trial conversions.

principles.text: Dynamically brand the product to each customer for a personal first impression and higher engagement.
principles.quote: By pulling a complete style guide via an API, you move from generic user interfaces to dynamically branded experiences that feel tailor-made for each customer.

principles.text: Cache API results instead of repeating identical calls, to improve performance and cut costs.
principles.quote: If you need brand data for the same company multiple times, cache the results in your own database or a temporary store. Fetch it once, then reuse it.

principles.text: Pick data vendors on accuracy and freshness first; trust in the data is the real value.
principles.quote: The real value of a company information API isn't just in the data it provides, but in the trust you can place in that data. Accuracy and reliability should be your top priorities during evaluation.

principles.text: Prefer transparent usage-based pricing that lets you start small and scale without a cost wall.
principles.quote: You want clear, usage-based pricing that lets you start small and scale up without hitting a cost wall.
